artifacts.summary: Phase 2 completion handoff: URL-recording curl stub, build_scratch lib copy, write_binding helper, and the pre-change negative control (case 18) added to test-sapience-capture.sh; next dispatch starts Phase 3.

completion_data.completion_summary: Extended test-sapience-capture.sh with a .curl_urls recorder (plus curl_urls readback helper) in build_curl_stub, a lib/sapience-api-lib.sh copy in build_scratch, a write_binding <scratch> <cid> helper mirroring test-sapience-remember.sh/test-sapience-publish.sh, and case 18: a pre-change negative control proving the UNMODIFIED sapience-retrieve.sh's request carries exactly the query parameters q/source/limit/token (no project_cid, no project), with source= verified against the fixture's own minted slug. All 18 cases / 46 assertions pass.

sapience_notes.subject: curl stub URL capture for sapience-retrieve.sh's test harness
sapience_notes.value: sapience-retrieve.sh's issue_request passes the fully-built URL as curl's final positional argument (`curl -sS --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 8 -H '...' -w $'\n%{http_code}' "$url"`), so a PATH-shadowing curl stub can record the exact request URL with `echo "${@: -1}" >> recorder_file` -- no argv parsing needed, and this is robust to any future flag added before the URL as long as the URL stays the last argument.

sapience_notes.subject: query-parameter-set assertions should test parameter NAMES, not substrings
sapience_notes.value: A negative control asserting a URL carries no project_cid/project parameter is safer as an exact match on the sorted set of parameter NAMES (split on '&', 'cut -d= -f1', sort) than as a string-containment grep for the absence of 'project_cid=' or 'project=' -- the name-set form cannot pass vacuously if an unrelated future parameter happens to contain the substring 'project'.

sapience_notes.subject: test-handoff-dispatch-identity.sh case2-mismatch-inside-window is a timing flake
sapience_notes.value: Under a verify-touched.sh batch run, test-handoff-dispatch-identity.sh's case2-mismatch-inside-window intermittently fails with an unexpected 'STALE HANDOFF' rejection message instead of the expected 'DISPATCH_SEQ MISMATCH' one -- an mtime-granularity race between the fixture's minted handoff mtime and the dispatch window boundary. Re-running the suite standalone immediately afterward passed 13/13, confirming this is a pre-existing timing flake unrelated to concurrent edits, not a regression signal.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience test-suite write_binding naming convention across suites
sapience_notes.value: test-sapience-remember.sh and test-sapience-publish.sh each independently define their own write_binding <scratch> <cid> helper with the identical three-key {project, name, repo} shape (repo = basename of the scratch dir). test-sapience-capture.sh now carries a THIRD copy under the same name for sapience-retrieve.sh's link-present cases, deliberately kept distinct from that file's own differently-shaped resolver_write_binding (which supports an extra fourth key for rejection cases) -- the two coexist because they serve different fixture shapes, not because of an oversight.
